- [ASSISTANT_CREATED] A kayak polo training session that takes about 1.5 hours for around 15 people, including warm-up, drills, game play, and cool-down.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Warm-Up (15 minutes): Begin with a 5-10 minute light paddle to warm up the muscles; follow with 5 minutes of stretching to increase flexibility and reduce the risk of injury.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Drills (45 minutes): Pass and Shoot, Blocking, Scrimmage.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Game Play (30 minutes): Set up two goals on opposite ends, divide into two teams of seven players each, play a game of kayak polo with two 15-minute halves, encourage practice of passing, shooting, and blocking skills, allow substitutions as needed.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Cool-Down (15 minutes): End with a 5-10 minute light paddle to cool down the muscles; follow with 5 minutes of stretching to improve flexibility and reduce the risk of injury.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Note: Establish clear boundaries for the playing area, set rules for safe play, wear appropriate safety gear including a properly fitting life jacket, and play in a calm and safe water environment.
- [ASSISTANT_CREATED] A whitewater kayak training session for total beginners on class 2 whitewater, including warm-up, safety briefing, flatwater skills practice, class 2 whitewater skills practice, and cool-down.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Warm-Up (10-15 minutes): Begin with a 5-10 minute light paddle to warm up the muscles; follow with 5 minutes of stretching to increase flexibility and reduce the risk of injury.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Safety Briefing (10-15 minutes): Cover basic safety information, including wearing a properly fitting life jacket and helmet, how to perform a wet exit, and how to swim in whitewater; discuss the importance of communication and staying together as a group; go over hand signals and basic river rescue techniques.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Flatwater Skills Practice (30-45 minutes): Practice basic paddle strokes, edging, bracing techniques, wet exits, and self-rescue techniques in flatwater.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Class 2 Whitewater Skills Practice (60-90 minutes): Begin with a short section of easy class 1 or flatwater to warm up; practice maneuvering through small waves and eddies, ferrying, catching and exiting eddies, running small drops and waves, and encourage group communication.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Cool-Down (10-15 minutes): End with a 5-10
